question: What is the primary purpose of healthcare data storytelling?

options.A: To increase the speed of routine drug administration
options.B: To replace patient medical records with computer graphs
options.C: To combine statistics with narrative context for action
options.D: To hide unfavorable hospital statistics from the public

explanation: Data storytelling uses numbers alongside a narrative to make clinical facts meaningful and drive change. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do raw clinical numbers often fail to convince hospital administrators on their own?

options.A: Raw data is always mathematically incorrect
options.B: They lack context and human resonance
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to view statistics
options.D: Administrators are unable to read spreadsheets

explanation: Numbers without a story fail to show the human impact behind the metrics. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h1)

question: Who requires a focus on financial savings and safety outcomes during a data presentation?
explanation: Upper management typically focuses on broader metrics like finances and overall safety indicators. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h2)

question: A nurse wants to convince hospital management to fund a new triage desk. What should be the primary focus of the data presentation?

options.A: Detailed biochemical formulas of common drugs
options.B: Financial savings and patient safety outcomes
options.D: Personal biographies of the ward staff

explanation: Administrative decision-makers respond best to metrics tied to organizational efficiency and safety. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h2)

question: What does tracking patient wait times primarily measure in a healthcare facility?

options.C: Efficiency in outpatient departments and emergency rooms
options.D: The total cost of surgical instruments per month

explanation: Wait times directly reflect how quickly patients move through triage and initial care areas. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which metric is most suitable for evaluating hand hygiene compliance and sterile procedure adherence?
explanation: Infection rates rise when sterile techniques and hand hygiene protocols are neglected. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the first step in structuring a compelling data narrative?

options.B: Writing a research paper for a foreign journal
options.C: Demanding immediate resignation of negligent staff
options.D: Establishing the context and baseline status

explanation: Every good data story begins by setting the baseline before introducing any problem or change. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is introducing a conflict or problem essential in a clinical data story?

options.A: It highlights the gap that needs urgent nursing intervention
options.B: It proves that management is entirely at fault
options.C: It creates unnecessary panic among junior health workers
options.D: It allows the speaker to lengthen the meeting time

explanation: Identifying the problem draws attention to the specific clinical gap requiring action. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which visual tool is best suited for showing changes or trends over time?
explanation: Line graphs clearly connect data points across sequential periods, showing progress or decline. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h5)

question: A nurse wants to compare malaria admission rates across four different hospital wards. Which chart type should be selected?
explanation: Bar charts provide a clear visual comparison between distinct categories like different hospital wards. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary danger of failing to translate data into actionable insights?

options.A: Patients will immediately notice errors in the spreadsheet
options.B: The hospital computer system will automatically crash
options.C: Valuable metrics remain unused while clinical problems persist
options.D: Nursing licenses will be revoked by the regulatory council

explanation: Data must lead to practical operational changes, otherwise collecting it serves no clinical purpose. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h6)

question: An audit reveals missed vital sign entries at night. What is the most appropriate way to translate this into an actionable insight?

options.A: Assume night nurses are sleeping on duty and issue a public warning
options.B: Stop recording vital signs altogether during night shifts
options.C: Increase the workload of day-shift nurses to compensate
options.D: Investigate systemic issues like shift overlap and equipment availability

explanation: Actionable insights look beyond simple blame to identify root operational causes. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is assuming correlation equals causation a dangerous pitfall in healthcare data?

options.A: It prevents nurses from writing accurate shift reports
options.B: It can lead to treating the wrong root cause of a clinical problem
options.C: It always results in immediate loss of hospital accreditation
options.D: It makes mathematical formulas impossible to calculate

explanation: Mistaking a coincidence for a direct cause wastes resources on ineffective interventions. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h7)

question: What does a small sample size often do to the reliability of clinical statistics?

options.A: It speeds up the process of data entry for nurses
options.B: It makes the data statistically insignificant or misleading
options.C: It eliminates all forms of human error in documentation
options.D: It guarantees absolute accuracy in patient outcomes

explanation: Small sample sizes can skew results, making them poor representations of broader clinical realities. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h7)
